I0.reason: RL post-training method (REPO) for a Qwen3-32B negotiation agent, evaluated by expert consensus on 30 online conversations and 45 curated bad cases against SFT/DPO/PPO/GRPO, plus a production A/B test on 9,653 conversations

1_n_items.unit: conversations (30 online, ~240 utterances; 45 bad cases, ~360 utterances; A/B 9,653 conversations, arm sizes not given)

2a_runs.loc: §5 p.4: 'We report the best-performing checkpoint'; no repeated runs

3_decoding.loc: §5 p.4: maximum response length 512 tokens; no temperature or sampling setting for evaluation

4_model_version.loc: §5 p.4: Qwen3-32B-Instruct; base Qwen2.5-32B; the supplementary 'GPT-based rater' (§7.2 p.6) and the reward judges (DeepSeek, GPT-5, App. tables) without snapshot or date

5_prompts.loc: App.: policy prompt Table 7, reward-judge prompt Fig. 6, GPT-based rater criteria Fig. 10 (p.8 onward)

6_uncertainty.kind: significance test (p < 0.001) for the production A/B test only; none for the expert evaluation

7_llm_judge.loc: §7.2 p.6: GPT-based rater for four binary conversational skills (supplementary); main evaluation by three human experts (§6 p.5)

8_judge_human_validation.loc: §6-7 p.5-6: no comparison of the GPT-based rater with the expert judgements

9a_agreement_metric.loc: as item 8; expert evaluation is a consensus ('conducted and agreed upon by three human experts'), no inter-expert agreement reported

10_contamination.loc: private production conversations (§5 p.4); contamination not discussed

11b_data.loc: proprietary production data; ethics statement p.6 does not release it

H1.sentence: REPO improves average dialogue rating to 4.63 (+0.33 over GRPO)
H1.metric: mean expert rating (1-5) on online conversations
H1.structure: paired (same conversations); utterances clustered within conversations

H1_alt_cell.sentence: raises the share of conversations with at least one excellent response to 66.67% (+23.34 pp over GRPO)
H1_alt_cell.metric: share of conversations with at least one excellent response

headline.H2: Production A/B test: response rate 46.72% -> 58.86% (+12.14 pp) and task success 19.32% -> 25.26% (+5.94 pp), p < 0.001, on 9,653 conversations (abstract; §6 p.5)

notes: The abstract's first comparison is a mean rating (not a proportion); its second is a proportion on n = 30 (run as the alternative cell). The A/B test is the only claim with a significance test.
